reference.title: Hollow Rock
reference.listing: Page could not be read here (gymvisual.com is blocked by the proxy); the movement is taken from the exercise name and standard coaching practice.

breathing.pattern: Short steady breaths behind a braced belly; do not hold the breath.
breathing.cadence: About one breath per two rocks

prescription.tempo: About 1 s per rock (back and forward)
prescription.progression: Hollow hold first (30 s), then short sets of rocks, then longer sets

cues.text: Lie on your back, arms overhead, legs together. Press the low back down.
Lift the shoulder blades and the straight legs into the hollow (banana) shape.
Keep the shape locked and rock back and forth: from the upper back to the low back and back.
Arms by the ears, legs together, toes pointed; the hips and shoulders never fold.
Stop, settle and lower to the mat.

mistakes.mistake: Folding at the hips to rock (piking)
mistakes.fix: Keep the angle between the trunk and the legs fixed; the whole body rocks.

mistakes.mistake: Low back arching on the forward rock
mistakes.fix: Tuck the pelvis more; regress to a smaller rock or a hollow hold.

mistakes.mistake: Throwing the arms or the head to make momentum
mistakes.fix: Arms stay by the ears; the rock comes from a small shift of the whole shape.

kinematics.norm: Low back pressed down (posterior tilt), shoulder blades and legs off the floor (Drysdale 2004; standard coaching cue)
The whole rigid shape rolls about 10-15 degrees each way along the curved back (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #14054, Hollow Rock, video (movement reference; page not readable here)
Drysdale, Earl and Hertel 2004, surface EMG of the abdominal muscles during pelvic-tilt and abdominal-hollowing exercises (J Athl Train 39(1):32-36)
Oliva-Lozano and Muyor 2020, core muscle activity during physical fitness exercises: a systematic review (Int J Environ Res Public Health 17(12):4306)

cautions: Stop if you feel sharp, radiating or nerve-type pain.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Holding the breath under effort raises blood pressure: keep breathing.
Needs a solid hollow hold first; rocking with an arching low back loads the lumbar spine.
modify: Low back arches: tuck the knees in or bring the arms to the sides.
Pregnancy, postpartum or diastasis recti: get cleared first, and avoid long supine work later in pregnancy.
progressions: Bigger, faster rocks with the shape held.

muscleNotes.core: Rectus abdominis and transversus abdominis lock the hollow shape (posterior pelvic tilt, ribs down) so the body rocks as one rigid curve; pelvic tilting with the legs unsupported drew the highest rectus abdominis and external oblique activity in Drysdale 2004, and V-sits reached about 80% MVIC of rectus abdominis (via Oliva-Lozano 2020).
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_r: Iliopsoas and rectus femoris hold the legs up against gravity (clinical opinion; Andersson 1997).
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_l: Iliopsoas and rectus femoris hold the legs up against gravity (clinical opinion; Andersson 1997).
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Assist rectus abdominis in keeping the ribs down and the pelvis tucked (Drysdale 2004).
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Assist rectus abdominis in keeping the ribs down and the pelvis tucked (Drysdale 2004).
muscleNotes.quads_r: Keep the knees straight and the legs long (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.quads_l: Keep the knees straight and the legs long (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Front deltoid holds the arms overhead by the ears (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Front deltoid holds the arms overhead by the ears (clinical opinion).

guides.label: Feet rise and fall as the body rocks
